body: The easiest way to serve AI apps and models - Build Model Inference APIs, Job queues, LLM apps, Multi-model pipelines, and more!
plain_description: Ship AI models as production-ready APIs in minutes. BentoML turns any model into a scalable REST or gRPC endpoint with just a few lines of Python — no infrastructure expertise required. The bottom line: you focus on model logic, BentoML handles serving, batching, Docker packaging, and cloud deployment.
technical_description: BentoML is a Python framework for building and serving AI/ML model inference APIs. It provides a decorator-based SDK to define services with standard Python type hints, automatically generating REST and gRPC endpoints with OpenAPI documentation. The framework includes built-in serving optimizations such as dynamic batching, model parallelism, multi-stage pipelines, and multi-model inference-graph orchestration. Services are packaged into standardized deployable artifacts called Bentos, which bundle code, models, and dependency configurations. BentoML generates Docker container images from Bentos and supports deployment to Kubernetes, BentoCloud, or any container orchestration platform. It integrates with any ML framework and inference runtime, and provides HTTP and gRPC clients for service interaction.
title: BentoML

body: Standardized Distributed Generative and Predictive AI Inference Platform for Scalable, Multi-Framework Deployment on Kubernetes
plain_description: KServe is one standardized platform for deploying all your AI models — from LLMs to traditional ML models — on Kubernetes without juggling multiple tools. It handles autoscaling, safe rollouts with traffic splitting, and built-in monitoring so your team can focus on improving models instead of managing infrastructure. The bottom line: faster, safer AI deployments at lower operational cost.
technical_description: KServe is a Kubernetes-native inference platform that provides a standardized InferenceService API for deploying generative and predictive AI models at scale. It supports multiple serving runtimes including vLLM for LLMs and native runtimes for TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn, XGBoost, and ONNX. The platform implements canary rollouts, request-based autoscaling with scale-to-zero, model explainability, payload logging, outlier and drift detection, and InferenceGraph for complex request routing. Client integration is via OpenAI-compatible REST and gRPC protocols. The control plane is implemented in Go with Python serving runtimes.
title: KServe

body: ncnn is a high-performance neural network inference framework optimized for the mobile platform
plain_description: Run AI models directly on mobile phones, desktops, and embedded devices without cloud servers. ncnn is the production-proven inference engine behind Tencent apps like WeChat and QQ — it delivers fast on-device AI with no external runtime dependencies. The bottom line: you can deploy deep learning models anywhere your application runs.
technical_description: ncnn is a high-performance neural network inference framework written in C++ with C and Python bindings. It targets mobile, embedded, and desktop platforms with CPU inference (ARM NEON, multi-core scheduling) and Vulkan GPU acceleration. The framework requires no third-party runtime dependencies and provides a low-memory blob/workspace allocator design. Model conversion from PyTorch and ONNX is handled by the bundled pnnx tool, with support for fp16 and int8 quantized inference paths.
title: ncnn

body: ONNX Runtime: cross-platform, high performance ML inferencing and training accelerator
plain_description: ONNX Runtime accelerates machine learning inference and training across virtually any hardware, reducing infrastructure costs and improving application responsiveness. It works with models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, and other major frameworks without requiring deep infrastructure changes. The result: faster ML performance in production with fewer resources.
technical_description: ONNX Runtime is a cross-platform inference and training engine for ONNX-format models. It applies graph-level optimizations and selects the optimal execution provider (CPU, CUDA, TensorRT, CoreML, OpenVINO, DirectML, WebGPU, and others) for the target hardware. The C++ core exposes C, Python, C#, Java, JavaScript, and Rust language bindings. Training acceleration integrates with existing PyTorch training scripts via a single-line API change, supporting multi-node NVIDIA GPU clusters with distributed data-parallel and mixed-precision training. The project includes quantization tooling and transformer-specific optimization pipelines for latency and throughput tuning in production.
title: ONNX Runtime

body: OpenVINO™ is an open source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference
plain_description: The big picture: OpenVINO lets you deploy AI models up to 40% faster across Intel hardware from edge devices to the cloud — without changing your code. Here's why it matters: You can take models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, or ONNX and run them on CPUs, GPUs, or NPUs with a single API. The bottom line: Less engineering time, lower infrastructure cost, and broader hardware compatibility for your AI workloads.
technical_description: OpenVINO is an open-source C++ toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning inference. It converts models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, TensorFlow Lite, PaddlePaddle, and JAX/Flax into an intermediate representation (IR) that is compiled and executed via a plugin architecture supporting CPU (x86, ARM), Intel GPU, and Intel NPU. The runtime offers C++, Python, C, and Node.js APIs, with a dedicated GenAI API for LLM pipelines. Post-training optimization is available through the NNCF library, including quantization, weight compression, and sparsity. Inference is performed locally with no cloud dependency after setup.
title: OpenVINO

body: Ray is an AI compute engine. Ray consists of a core distributed runtime and a set of AI Libraries for accelerating ML workloads.
plain_description: Ray lets you scale AI and Python applications from a laptop to a cluster without rewriting your code. It provides a unified runtime for distributed training, serving, tuning, and data processing — so teams can move from prototype to production faster without managing separate infrastructure.
technical_description: Ray is a unified distributed runtime for scaling AI and Python workloads. It provides a core distributed scheduler with task, actor, and object abstractions, plus a set of AI libraries: Ray Serve for model serving, Ray Train for distributed training, Ray Tune for hyperparameter tuning, Ray Data for scalable datasets, and RLlib for reinforcement learning. Ray runs on any machine, cluster, cloud provider, or Kubernetes, and is installable via pip. It features a dashboard for monitoring and debugging, and supports integrations with the broader ML ecosystem.
title: Ray

body: An MLOps framework to package, deploy, monitor and manage thousands of production machine learning models
plain_description: Seldon Core 2 gives you a standardized way to deploy and manage AI systems on Kubernetes, from single models to complex modular applications. The big picture: deploy across model types, on-prem or in any cloud, production-ready out of the box. Here's why it matters: save infrastructure costs with multi-model serving and overcommit, run A/B experiments, and build composable pipelines with realtime data streaming.
technical_description: Seldon Core 2 is an open-source MLOps and LLMOps framework for deploying, managing, and scaling AI applications on Kubernetes. It provides a unified control plane with a scheduler, model gateway, pipeline gateway, and dataflow engine that orchestrate model serving and inference pipelines. The framework leverages Apache Kafka for realtime data streaming between composable pipeline components and supports multi-model serving on shared inference servers with autoscaling and overcommit capabilities. Integration is via Kubernetes custom resources (CRDs), a CLI, and the V2 Dataplane inference protocol. Additional capabilities include experiment management for A/B testing and shadow deployments, drift and outlier detection, and custom component integration through a plug-in architecture.
title: Seldon Core 2

body: The Triton Inference Server provides an optimized cloud and edge inferencing solution.
plain_description: The big picture: Deploy and serve any AI model in production with optimized performance across cloud, data center, and edge. Here's why it matters: Triton supports models from all major frameworks (PyTorch, ONNX, TensorRT, and more) on NVIDIA GPUs, CPUs, or AWS Inferentia. The bottom line: It handles real-time, batched, and streaming inference with built-in dynamic batching and model pipelining — no infrastructure rewrites needed.
technical_description: Triton Inference Server is an open-source inference serving solution providing a unified serving infrastructure for AI models across multiple frameworks and hardware platforms. It exposes HTTP/REST and gRPC endpoints based on the KServe protocol, supporting concurrent model execution, dynamic and sequence batching, model ensembles, and Business Logic Scripting (BLS). The server runs in Docker containers with backends for TensorRT, PyTorch, ONNX, OpenVINO, Python, and RAPIDS FIL, and includes model management APIs, GPU utilization and latency metrics, response caching, and client libraries in C++, Python, and Java.
title: Triton Inference Server
